title: MulSTE: A Multi-view Spatio-temporal Learning Framework with Heterogeneous Event Fusion for Demand-supply Prediction

problem.claim: Predicting purchase demand and delivery supply capacity is important for streamlining integrated logistics operations and improving efficiency.

gap.claim: Existing joint demand-supply prediction studies seldom address the impacts of diverse events.

contributions.claim: MulSTE is a multi-view spatio-temporal learning framework with heterogeneous event fusion for demand-supply prediction.
The Event Fusion Representation module fuses textual, numerical, and categorical information for emergent and periodic events.

The framework includes a multi-graph adaptive convolution recurrent network as a spatio-temporal encoder and an event-gated demand-supply interaction attention module for modeling demand-supply interactions during events.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The evaluation used two real-world datasets obtained from JD Logistics and public websites.
The authors report that their method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across various metrics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Integrated warehouse and distribution logistics systems are used to respond to changing customer demand.
Joint prediction of purchase demand and delivery supply capacity is presented as a crucial operational problem.
Demand-supply interactions are affected by economic relationships and event-driven consumer psychology, while prior studies seldom address diverse events.
MulSTE combines heterogeneous event fusion, spatio-temporal encoding, and event-aware demand-supply interaction modeling.
The authors report evaluations on two real-world datasets and improved performance over state-of-the-art baselines across various metrics.

source_observation.claim: The framework fuses textual, numerical, and categorical event information with demand-supply and spatio-temporal modeling.

interpretation.claim: Prediction systems may benefit from representing heterogeneous event signals alongside the primary operational variables.

application.claim: For demand-supply forecasting, incorporate event representations and event-conditioned interaction modeling when event effects are operationally relevant.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach is beneficial outside the reported logistics and event settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the dataset names, sizes, time spans, or task split details.
The abstract does not identify the evaluation metrics or report numerical results.
The abstract does not provide implementation, training, or ablation details.
